issues.legal_issue: An auction bid that is expressly subject to confirmation does not create a completed sale before confirmation.
material_facts: The highest bid was made subject to confirmation by the Chief Commissioner, who could reject it.
The Chief Commissioner did not confirm the bid.
issues.conclusion: The sale was not complete without confirmation, and the bidder could withdraw the bid before confirmation without incurring liability for breach of contract or a resale shortfall.
issues.legal_principle: Under clause 33 of the auction conditions, final bids were subject to the Chief Commissioner's confirmation; clause 16 of Rule 5.34 also made sales open to revision by the Chief Commissioner. A conditional acceptance does not conclude a contract, and the offer may be withdrawn before absolute acceptance. The Court relied on Hussey v. Horne Payne, [1878] 8 Ch. D. 670 at 676.

predicates.conditional_auction_contract_dispute: The proceeding concerns whether an auction bid created a binding contract.
predicates.bid_subject_to_confirmation: The auction terms made the bid subject to confirmation by an authority.
predicates.confirmation_not_given: The authority did not confirm the bid.

issues.definition: When a contract dispute concerns a bid made subject to confirmation and confirmation is not given, there is no completed sale contract before confirmation.

issues.legal_issue: A bidder is not liable for a resale price deficiency where the auction sale was subject to confirmation and no completed sale resulted.
material_facts: The bidder did not pay the required deposit after the auction.
The Chief Commissioner did not confirm the bid, and the licence was resold at a lower price.
The Collector sought to recover the difference between the bids from the original bidder.
issues.conclusion: The original bidder was not liable for the resale deficiency because the sale had not been completed.
issues.legal_principle: Clause 21 of Rule 5.34 distinguishes a person to whom a shop has been sold from a bidder whose bid has only been provisionally accepted. Its first part concerns a completed sale; its later part expressly addresses an auction conducted by an officer lower in rank than the Collector and permits recovery of a deficiency from a defaulting bidder in that situation. Because the sale here required confirmation and was not confirmed, the essential prerequisites of a completed sale were absent. Clause 33 of the auction conditions made bids subject to confirmation.

rule.if: resale_deficiency_recovery_dispute and auction_sale_subject_to_confirmation and confirmation_not_given and resale_deficiency_claimed

predicates.resale_deficiency_recovery_dispute: The proceeding concerns recovery from an auction bidder of a price deficiency following resale.
predicates.auction_sale_subject_to_confirmation: The auction terms required confirmation before the sale became complete.
predicates.confirmation_not_given: The authority did not confirm the bidder's bid.
predicates.resale_deficiency_claimed: A deficiency arose on resale and recovery of it was sought from the original bidder.

issues.definition: In a dispute over recovery of a resale deficiency, a bidder whose sale required confirmation is not liable for the deficiency if confirmation was not given.
